quote: I didn't fill out any solar form, but I wouldn't be surprised if my wife did.
stewart_read: Rep opened for 'Jamie' and got a different person entirely disclaiming the form; rep never re-anchors legitimacy for THIS person before continuing the script.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as the rep smoothly adapting mid-call, but the transcript shows no explicit re-legitimizing line — just an abrupt pivot to estimate questions.
coaching_implication: When the named contact isn't who filled out the form, take 10 seconds to confirm who you're speaking to and why they're a valid participant before running verify.

quote: Well, I just had a few questions to get started on the estimate. Is that correct? What are your questions?
stewart_read: Interest question is skipped entirely per verified events — rep jumps straight to address verification without ever asking what interested him in solar.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the confused opening (wrong-contact mixup) as not the moment for rapport-building, deferring interest capture — but it's never picked up later either.
coaching_implication: Interest capture is the emotional anchor for the whole call; skipping it removes the only hook available for the bill-flip or a personalized text follow-up.

quote: Do you know how much you're spending on a monthly average?
stewart_read: This is touch 1 of the bill-collection friction pattern — asked cleanly but customer can't answer immediately.
coaching_implication: First ask is fine; the issue is what happens after (see following touches).

quote: My bills over the last year are between 155 and 196.
stewart_read: The bill number lands and the rep responds with a flat acknowledgment token, filing it rather than reflecting it back as a hook.
coaching_implication: A one-line flip here ('so you're paying that every month whether you use it or not') would set up the appointment framing later — never happens.

stewart_read: Third touch of the same bill-collection struggle — rep finally gets the graph via text/screenshot workaround after ~5 minutes of navigation coaching.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as good persistence rather than failure — rep did eventually secure the document rather than abandoning it.
coaching_implication: The persistence paid off procedurally, but a pivot to verbal read-back at minute 2-3 would have saved several minutes for the same result.

quote: seeing the way it stands, what the local geometry and geography are, how it points with respect to north and south. All those little details are very important.
stewart_read: Customer, a self-described engineer/physicist, volunteers technically sophisticated reasoning for wanting an in-person visit — this is an engaged, technically-curious lead.
coaching_implication: Rep handled this fine by booking the in-person visit, but never verbally acknowledged or leaned into his technical enthusiasm ('you clearly know your stuff, the consultant will get into all of that') which could have deepened buy-in.

quote: K. Let me just take a look. Monday. You said noon to two, so not that. Not that. Yeah. Not that. Ten ten to eleven, you know, I can do it through. To eleven.
stewart_read: Time is worked out live and appears locked (10-11 Monday) but the button_up is thin — no 'is that fair' handshake, no one-hour-block or no-driving language captured.
coaching_implication: Booking mechanics landed a real day+time but skipped the confirmation elements that predict show-rate; coach to always close with the fair-handshake line.
